A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VideoTIR study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables that support reliable matching. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix, despite referring to separate supplementary material that is unavailable in the supplied files.

before.justification: v1 reports original VideoTIR benchmark results, SFT and routing analyses, and TAGPO-versus-GRPO experiments in Section 4, Tables 1–5 and Figure 8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports VideoTIR inference latency and average tool invocations in its new Table 3.

M1.justification: The textual router, hierarchical retrieval toolkit, TAGPO update and trajectory-synthesis pipeline are unchanged. Changing 'external' to 'internal' tools in the long-form results discussion aligns that passage with the method already described in v1.

E1.justification: The training sources and MVBench, Video-MME and LongVideoBench evaluations are retained. The added efficiency comparison identifies no new dataset, task, population or input scenario.

E2.justification: New v3 Table 3 introduces an efficiency comparison against VideoMA, COLT and VideoMTR. VideoMA and COLT were not evaluated comparators in v1, while VideoMTR already appeared in the accuracy comparison. Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added efficiency experiment reports inference-time invocation counts and end-to-end latency excluding network overhead; comparator call counts are marked as manually set by the original papers. Existing benchmark splits, model configurations, training budgets and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused analysis of how toolkit design relates to inference cost in Section 4.3 and Table 3. The existing formatting, Normal-SFT versus Random-SFT, router-selection and TAGPO analyses are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-level variability. Existing rollout and data-curation repetition counts are unchanged, and the new efficiency table adds no repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation results and training curves are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. New v3 Table 3 reports calls/latency of 3/27.4s for VideoMA, 3/68.3s for COLT, 2/5.9s for VideoMTR and 1.42/4.6s for VideoTIR. These are additional comparisons, not performance improvements over v1's VideoTIR results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same episode reward, decayed per-call reward, tool-specific advantage normalization and composite policy-gradient update. The accompanying mathematical examples are unchanged; no theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: an internal multi-tool framework, TAGPO and sandbox-based trajectory synthesis. The efficiency comparison supplies additional support for an existing claim rather than changing its scope.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 attributes inference efficiency to avoiding inter-process overhead and enabling GPU parallelization through the internal toolkit. The long-form results discussion also corrects its characterization of the tools as external. Existing interpretations and failure explanations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new efficiency table supplies limited comparator implementation details: VideoMA uses GPT-4o/Gemini API calls, and COLT uses eight external specialist models. Existing VideoTIR hardware, hyperparameters, training frameworks, data preparation and resource-access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds COLT as a cited work and extends the efficiency positioning against external-tool systems. Duplicate bibliography entries for VideoAgent and DrVideo are consolidated without removing those works; the broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized spelling, grammar and heading corrections, updates author information and running headers, and adds acknowledgements. It inserts an Efficiency Analysis subsection before the retained ablations, while preserving the overall narrative and section organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds efficiency Table 3, rearranges the formatting table, and enlarges the retained SFT comparison into full-width Table 4. Later tables are relocated and renumbered, Figure 8a is reduced in size, and citation styling changes. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 and Section 4.3 make the existing inference-efficiency claim more assessable through explicit latency and invocation-count evidence, while wording corrections and the revised ablation layout improve readability. The gain is limited: the timing dataset and per-method model/hardware controls are insufficiently specified to establish a rigorously matched speed advantage. The method and existing accuracy evidence remain unchanged.
